answer: A falcon is registered in the inlet only when three sponsors who share no sponsor within two hops each lock saffron behind it, and a sponsor's k-th live falcon costs it k² saffron, slashed if that falcon is proven a duplicate. The inlet stores the full sponsor graph, so clones vouched for by one ring collide there and are voided. An honest newcomer costs its three backers 1 saffron each, but a ring of 30 sponsors backing 1,000 falcons locks about 10 million saffron. It breaks if unrelated sponsors can be bribed or rented cheaply.
